chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, the servant asks Allah for a need, and it may be that its fulfillment is to occur for him after a near term or after a delayed time. Then the servant commits a sin, so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says to the angel: "Do not fulfill his need, and deprive him of it, for he has exposed himself to My anger and has deserved deprivation from Me."

key_terms.الْحَاجَةَ: the need or request being asked from Allah
key_terms.الْحِرْمَانَ: deprivation; being denied a blessing or request
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ: the servant; the human being in relation to Allah as His servant
key_terms.ذَنْبًا: a sin committed by the servant
key_terms.لِسَخَطِي: to My anger; indicating divine displeasure

ai.seo_question: Can sins prevent a person's du'a from being answered?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a person's sins can become a cause for being deprived of blessings and the fulfillment of needs he has asked Allah for. It underscores the ethical and spiritual link between obedience, du'a, and divine response.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The servant asks Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for the need, and it happens to be from his status for it to be Fulfilled to a near term or a longer term. So the servant commits a sin, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High is Saying to the Angel: “Do not fulfil his need and deprive him of it, for he has been exposed to My<sup>azwj</sup> Anger and it Obligates the deprivation from Me<sup>azwj</sup>”’.
en.sarwar: 14. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

‘‘When a servant (of Allah) prays, his prayer is supposed to be answered within a short or a longer time. The servant (of Allah) commits a sin and Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, says to the angel not to answer his prayer and deprive him; he is subjected to My anger and he deserves deprivation from Me.”
